design:
Tier 2: one nullable column with a backfill, applied to the operator's :8000 database at its next restart.

D1. The decision is made at launch, in trigger_agent_directly, not in the rebind. Every turn passes through it: manual, queued, job and peer (agent_trigger.py:1124-1131). The CLI can also change without PATCH seeing the old one: a PATCH may set runner_id to null (agents.py:3245-3251), and deleting a runner unbinds the archived agents that held it (runners.py:295-305), so the later bind has no previous CLI to compare with. And conversations the PATCH never looks at (a job's, an inherited one) carry the same state. agents.py:3244-3251 is unchanged. A runner's CLI cannot change after it is created (runners.py:196-227 reads runner.cli), so the CLI is the right thing to compare.

D2. Which CLI a session belongs to is recorded, not derived: a new conversations.provider_session_cli (String(32), nullable) beside provider_session_id. It is written only with that column, through one helper in conversations.py (set_provider_session(conversation, session_id, cli)). Every current writer goes through it: agent_trigger.py:2262 (typed session, cli unknown), :3470 and :4467 (binding at a run, the run's CLI), :4449 and inbound_queue.py:502 (clears), output_recording.py:114 (self-reported, unknown) and scheduler.py:4508 (a job's stored id, unknown). A ratchet test refuses `.provider_session_id =` anywhere else. Rejected: deriving it from turn_usage.runner, which makes an accounting row decide execution and depends on which runs completed; F1023's two failed Claude runs recorded runner claude while the session was Copilot's. Rejected: clearing every conversation's session at PATCH (D1).

D3. A crossing is when a session is set, its CLI is known and it differs from the bound runner's cli. The launch then uses no resume id and session_mode 'new', and clears the session through the helper in the same commit as the Run row (agent_trigger.py:2020-2032), so a refused start changes nothing. The old id has to be cleared, because the first-writer rule (agent_trigger.py:3469-3479, :4466-4476) would otherwise refuse the new session after the turn ran. The sentence goes into setup_events (recorded before the runner's output on all three transports, agent_trigger.py:3245, :3272, :3545) and into the prompt's notices, the shape the dependency-link notice uses (agent_trigger.py:1758-1772). An unknown CLI is resumed as today, and Copilot's -32002 rescue and the queue's give-up stay as the backstop.

D4. Model: model_catalog.py gains one function answering whether a stored model applies to a CLI: it does when that CLI declares it (ProviderDescriptor.model, which accepts aliases, model_catalog.py:149-155) or when no CLI declares it. agent_trigger.py:1197-1198 uses it on the non-provider branch; the provider branch (:1191-1196, D7) is unchanged. A withheld model is kept on the conversation, not removed. The composer re-sends the stored overrides with each message (AgentOutputPanel.tsx:323-333), and validate_overrides accepts an undeclared model only when it equals the stored one (model_catalog.py:688-694), so removing it would get the operator's next message refused with a 400. Keeping it also means rebinding back restores the model. The 'declared by no CLI' clause keeps a retired model working where it is stored (the-copilot-catalog-tracks-the-cli, D2). Shared ids such as claude-sonnet-5, which both Claude and Copilot declare, simply apply. The runner.model_withheld diagnostic is recorded on new-session turns only, so it is said once per session.

D5. Nothing new is recorded about the model. run_started already carries the launch's model (agent_trigger.py:3378-3386, :4420-4429) and turn_usage.model is the CLI's report (usage_accounting.py:58; runner_parsing.py:166-190 for Claude; copilot_usage.py for Copilot). Once D4 stops passing a foreign model, the two agree.

D6. Migration (next free revision after 0147; slices C and K also touch hub/hub/db, so take the number at build time). It adds the column, guarded for a missing table, and backfills it for conversations holding a session: the turn_usage.runner of the latest run in that conversation with status 'completed' and session_id equal to the conversation's provider_session_id, else NULL. Hazard: it writes to every row of the operator's conversations table at their next :8000 restart. Back up the database first (operator authorised migrations on 2026-10-27, with a backup). Rollback: the downgrade drops the column in a batch; a reverted Hub never reads it, and no other value is changed.

D7. UI (task 2): the composer applies D4's rule from the model catalog it already loads, next to overridesForRunner (runnerProvider.ts:27-35, which already hides a model a provider runner ignores). It is a display rule only, and the backend stays the authority.

open_questions.question: Should a stored model the new CLI does not offer be removed from the conversation or kept? Decided: kept and withheld, as the provider branch's D7 does. Removing it would get the composer's next message refused (D4).

Should the rebind (PATCH) clear the agent's conversations' sessions instead of the launch deciding? Decided: the launch decides, because an unbind or a deleted runner followed by a new bind gives the PATCH no previous CLI and jobs and inherited conversations bypass it (D1).

problem: Found by the day sweep of 2026-10-23 on scratch Hub :8117 (scripts/drive/s1023_rm_rebind.py, s1023_rm_turn.py, s1023_rm_jobdoor2.py). F1023: agent a-run had two Claude turns in conv-f45e1b5b2180; rebound to a Copilot runner it was asked to load Claude's session 62f1c78b (Copilot alone recovers, copilot_acp.py:2700-2721); rebound back to Claude, run-48eb218457b6 and run-e6eee0b7e373 failed with 'No conversation found with session ID: b36d6aef...' (Copilot's id) and only run-d079343e0501 succeeded, on a fresh session nobody was told about. The operator sent one message and saw two failed turns and four copies of an error naming an id Claude never issued. F1024: the same conversation stored runtime_overrides {'model': 'haiku'}; after the rebind the Copilot run started with model 'haiku' (run_started), Copilot ran claude-sonnet-5 on a premium request, and the timeline reads 'Run started (copilot, haiku)'. The operator chose the cheapest model and paid for the plan default. The same stored value is copied into a job's or a peer message's new conversation (conversations.py:66-111), so the job door reproduces it with no rebind in sight. Moving agents between Claude and Copilot is how the operator balances the weekly Claude window against Copilot's premium requests, so this is hit by ordinary use, not by an edge case.

requirements.rationale: F1023: the launch resumes conversation.provider_session_id whatever CLI wrote it (agent_trigger.py:1277-1278), and only Copilot survives being handed a foreign id.
requirements.statement: A turn resumes the conversation's provider session only when that session is recorded as created by the CLI of the agent's bound runner. When it is recorded as another CLI's, the turn starts a new session: a Claude launch carries no --resume, a Codex exec launch no 'resume <id>', and a Copilot turn is given no session to load.

requirements.rationale: The first-writer rule refuses a second session while the old id is stored (agent_trigger.py:3469-3479 for the stream path, :4466-4476 for app-server and Copilot), so skipping the resume without clearing the old id would fail the turn after it ran.
requirements.statement: On a turn that starts a new session because the session was another CLI's, the conversation gives up that session before the run starts, so the session the new CLI creates becomes the conversation's without a binding conflict, and the next turn on the same CLI resumes it.

requirements.rationale: Only a session known to be another CLI's is given up; an unknown one keeps today's path, whose failure the queue's give-up already ends (inbound_queue.py:496-502).
requirements.statement: A turn resumes the conversation's session as today when the agent was rebound to another runner of the same CLI (for example a Claude runner with another model) or to the same runner, and when the session's CLI is unknown (not backfilled, typed by the operator, a job's stored id, or self-reported).

requirements.rationale: F1023: the third run answered from an empty session and nothing said so. The agent needs it as much as the operator: the conversation it is shown continuing is one it has no memory of.
requirements.statement: A turn that starts a new session because the agent now runs on another CLI records one info diagnostic (code runner.session_not_carried) in the conversation, before anything the runner emits, and prepends the same sentence to the agent's prompt. The sentence names the agent, the CLI the earlier turns ran on and the CLI it runs on now, and says the earlier turns are not in the new session. A turn that resumes records none.

requirements.rationale: F1024. The 'declared by no CLI' clause keeps a retired model working where it is stored (the-copilot-catalog-tracks-the-cli, D2). Kept, as the provider branch already keeps one (agent_trigger.py:1191-1196, design D7).
requirements.statement: On a runner with no model provider, a model stored on the conversation is applied only when the bound runner's CLI declares it (by id or alias) or when no CLI in the model catalog declares it. Otherwise the turn launches with the runner's own model, and the stored model stays on the conversation, so a turn after rebinding back to its CLI applies it again.

requirements.rationale: Said once per session, not on every turn: the composer's pill (the-composer-shows-what-will-run) carries it after that.
requirements.statement: A turn that starts a new session while a stored model is withheld records one info diagnostic (code runner.model_withheld) naming the stored model, the CLI that does not offer it and the model the turn runs on. Resumed turns of that session do not repeat it.

requirements.rationale: F1024: the Hub's own record said 'haiku' for a turn Copilot ran on claude-sonnet-5.
requirements.statement: A turn's run_started event, and the timeline's 'Run started (runner, model)' line, name the model the CLI was launched with, and its turn_usage row names the model the CLI reported. After a rebind to another CLI, neither names a model that only the previous CLI declares.

requirements.rationale: The roadmap's done sentence for slice J.
requirements.statement: In one conversation, a Claude agent rebound to a Copilot runner and then back to Claude runs one turn on each binding, each completing on its first delivery: no run fails, no queue entry is redelivered, and each turn's recorded model is one its own CLI ran.

requirements.rationale: Without a backfill every conversation on the operator's Hub would be unknown, and the first rebind after the upgrade would still fail as F1023 did.
requirements.statement: The migration records, for each existing conversation that holds a provider session, the runner recorded on that conversation's latest completed run that bound the same session id. It leaves the CLI unknown when there is no such run. Its downgrade removes the column and changes nothing else.

requirements.rationale: F1024 expected: 'the composer's model pill reads what will run'. The pill is seeded from the stored overrides (AgentOutputPanel.tsx:323-333).
requirements.statement: When the conversation's stored model would be withheld on the agent's bound runner, the composer's model pill shows the runner's model and says the conversation's model is not offered by that CLI. Sending a message from the composer leaves the stored model on the conversation.

in_scope: Recording, beside conversations.provider_session_id, the CLI whose session it is, through one helper used by every writer, and a migration that adds and backfills it
The launch decision in trigger_agent_directly: a session of another CLI is given up and a new one started, said once in the conversation and in the agent's prompt
The launch's model resolution for runners without a model provider: a stored model the bound CLI does not declare is withheld (kept on the conversation), said on a new-session turn
The composer's model pill showing the model the next turn runs on when the stored one is withheld
Stubbed tests through POST /agent/trigger for Claude, Copilot and Codex, and an operator drive with the real Claude and Copilot CLIs
non_goals: Carrying the earlier turns' content into the new CLI's session (a transcript replay or an automatic checkpoint hand-off). The new session starts empty and both the operator and the agent are told; the operator can take a checkpoint before rebinding.
Stored control overrides (effort, permission_mode): the catalog read on 2026-10-27 gives all three CLIs both controls with the same values, except that Codex has no 'max' effort. They are unchanged.

Changing what PATCH /agents/{name} does or answers (agents.py:3244-3251), F1026's unarchive message (slice I) and F1025's Manager model menu: a rebind stays a binding change, and the conversation decision is the launch's.
Removing Copilot's -32002 rescue (copilot_acp.py:2700-2721) or the queue's resume give-up (inbound_queue.py:404, :496-502): they stay as the backstop for sessions whose CLI is unknown.

Attributing a session the operator types (POST /agent/trigger session_mode 'resume', agent_trigger.py:2251-2263), a job's stored last_session_id (scheduler.py:4504-4509) or a self-reporting agent's session (output_recording.py:107-116): their CLI stays unknown, and they resume as today.
Driving Codex for real: it cannot be driven on this machine, so it is covered by the stubbed test only.

summary: A conversation's provider session is resumed only by the CLI that created it, and a per-conversation model is applied only when the bound runner's CLI offers it. Today a rebind to another CLI leaves both in place: Copilot is asked to load a Claude session and run Claude's 'haiku', and after the rebind back Claude fails the operator's turn twice on Copilot's session id before the queue silently drops it (F1023, F1024). The Hub records which CLI a conversation's session belongs to (one nullable column, backfilled), decides at launch, the one point every turn passes through, whether the session can be resumed, and withholds a stored model the bound CLI does not offer, saying both in the conversation and to the agent. The turn's recorded model is then the one the CLI was launched with, and its usage row keeps the model the CLI reported.
